what_its_for: Desoximetasone is a strong steroid cream, gel, ointment, or spray that you put on your skin. It helps reduce redness, itching, swelling, and irritation caused by skin conditions like eczema, psoriasis, rashes, and other inflammatory skin problems.
how_to_take: Wash and dry the affected skin area first. Apply a thin layer of the cream, gel, ointment, or spray to the affected area and gently rub it in. Wash your hands after applying, unless you are treating your hands. Do not cover the treated area with bandages or wrap it tightly unless your doctor tells you to. Do not use this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. Avoid getting it on healthy skin around the treated area.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area 1 to 2 times per day, or exactly as your doctor instructed. Do not use more than prescribed or apply it more often than directed. Do not use this medicine for longer than your doctor recommends, usually no more than 2 to 4 weeks without a follow-up visit.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra medicine to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tube, jar, or bottle tightly closed. Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not freeze. For the spray form, keep away from open flames or heat sources, as the spray is flammable.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using this medicine on your face, groin, or underarm areas unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Do not use it on open wounds, infected skin, or near your eyes. Avoid wrapping the treated area tightly with bandages without doctor approval, as this can increase the amount of medicine absorbed into your body and raise the risk of side effects. Do not use this medicine in larger amounts or for a longer time than prescribed.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice: skin irritation, burning, stinging, or worsening of your condition; signs of a skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, or pus; unusual weight gain, puffiness, or stretch marks; skin thinning, discoloration, or bruising easily; acne or increased hair growth on the treated area; or if your child shows signs of slowed growth. Seek emergency help if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice improvement in redness, itching, and irritation within a few days of starting treatment. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks to see the full benefit. Continue using it as directed even if you feel better. If your symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Use with extra caution in children. Children are more likely to absorb the medicine through their skin, which can cause side effects like slowed growth or hormonal changes. Use the smallest amount needed for the shortest time possible. Avoid using it in the diaper area. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Use only if clearly needed and prescribed by your doctor. If breastfeeding, do not apply this medicine to your chest or nipple area. Elderly patients: Use with caution, as older adults may have thinner skin and be more sensitive to side effects.
